data.name: Bhargavas
data.gender_notes: Bhargavas is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhargavas is a name derived from Bhargava, which is a gotra or clan name in Hinduism. It is associated with the sage Bhargava, who was a descendant of the great sage Bhrigu. The name Bhargavas carries the meaning “Derived from Bhargava” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhargavas usually hope their child will grow to embody derived from bhargava and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bhargavas holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it is associated with the Bhargava gotra or clan. In Hindu society, gotra is an important aspect of one's cultural identity and lineage. Being a Bhargava signifies a connection to this ancient and respected lineage of sages and scholars. The name Bhargavas also carries the legacy of the great sage Bhargava, who is revered for his wisdom and knowledge in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Bhargavas represents a deep connection to the spiritual heritage and wisdom of the Hindu tradition. The name itself carries the blessings and wisdom of the ancient sage Bhargava, who was known for his deep spiritual practices and connection to the divine. Bhargavas can be seen as a reminder to always seek knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual growth, just as the great sage Bhargava did. The name can serve as a source of inspiration and motivation for those seeking to deepen their spiritual practice and connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhargavas: Sages named Bhargava, hailed from the Himalayas. In spirituality, they embodied wisdom, penance, and devotion towards Lord Shiva. Their lives served as beacons of enlightenment, inspiring seekers on their own spiritual journeys.

vedic_reference.note: From the Vedas. Bhṛgu is a sage in the Vedas, and Bhargavas is his son.

historical_references.reference: Rigveda 1.171.2 refers to Bhargava Agastya, one of the sages who visited King Sudas and prophesied the coming of Indra's defeat by the god Vritra.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian text from the Rigveda era

historical_references.reference: In Mahabharata (Anushasana Parva), Bhargava Vyasa is mentioned as the author and narrator of the great epic, and he is also known as Vedavyasa due to his mastery over the Vedas.
